messages:
maria: Heads-up — deploy-bot just flagged the us-west1 hosted-api canary: p95 latency +25% vs baseline. I think we should do a manual rollback and pin until we have a root cause. Anyone object?

deploy-bot: [ALERT] Canary threshold exceeded (p95 latency). Baseline: 180ms -> 225ms (+25%). Auto-rollback candidate flagged. Auto actions suppressed due to current change window policy.

ashley: I can look at infra first. Any error-rate spike or just latency?

maria: errors are flat, just latency and some 503 retries on a small subset (kvcache hits dropping).

devon: might be KV cache eviction pattern with latest runtime kernels. We saw similar after the kernel tweak last night. If so, rollback model version or the kernel flag? Which is less risky?

sam: For customer stability, pin to last known-good model + rollout rollback. Pin + manual rollback is quickest. We can disable the new kernel flag in dedicated clusters later for a safe test.

ashley: agree with pin + rollback. I'll open a quick postmortem ticket and start metrics snapshotting.

maria: OK. Proposed rollback target: hosted-api -> model v3.1.2 (previous canary). Can someone run the rollback command? I don't want autopilot to do it without ops in loop.

devon: I'll run it and stay on the bridge. Command:
```
redwoodctl rollout --service hosted-api --to-model v3.1.2 --strategy immediate --reason "canary p95 spike"
```

deploy-bot: Deploy window notice: manual rollback will bypass gradual canary. Ensure oncall present.

sam: Oncall present — I'm on the bridge. maria, please post the customer-facing blurb once we pin. We'll send to CS and trust & safety.

maria: Draft for CS notice: "We observed a latency regression in a recent canary deployment affecting some US region requests. We've rolled back to a prior stable model to restore normal latency. No customer data was affected. We're investigating and will share an update within 2 hours." Thoughts?

ashley: fine. Add an apology line and brief ETA for update.

maria: updated: "... will share an update within 2 hours. Apologies for the disruption."

devon: executing the command now, monitoring logs.

(devon runs command)

deploy-bot: [ACTION] Rollout started by devon -> target v3.1.2. Traffic shifting: 100% immediate.

sam: seeing p95 trending down already in the first minute.

ashley: kvcache hit-rate back to expected range on the affected hosts. Looks like regression tied to the kernel patch.

maria: Pining note for release history: "2026-03-23: manual rollback to v3.1.2 due to canary p95 latency spike after kernel tweak. Customer notice sent."

devon: Rollback completed. All checks green. Leaving the bridge for postmortem writeup but will keep monitoring for 30m.

maria: Thanks. Next steps: devon to open a runtime-flag PR to revert last-night kernel tweak on canary-only, eng-ml to run a targeted perf test, and product to hold version bump until we validate. I'll assign follow-ups.

sam: I'll notify CS / trust channels with the blurb. Legal wants a heads-up; pinging them now.

maria: Great — closing thread once the 30m monitoring window passes. :thumbsup:
